_comment: Ratchet floor for scripts/dcp_chapter_measure.py. NOT_OK and UNMEASURED may go DOWN, never UP. This is not an acceptance of the defects it records - it is the floor that lets a fail-closed check go live without taking the product dark against chapters already known bad. ratchet.per_council is EMPTY until a first four-signal run is reviewed and recorded with --record-baseline; until then every key reports NO_BASELINE, which is not a pass.

frozen_signal1.frozen_by: user instruction: freeze today's counts as the ratchet baseline
frozen_signal1.signal: codes listed on the source PDF contents page vs codes we serve
frozen_signal1.NOT_COMPARABLE_WARNING: These numbers came from ONE signal and a NARROWER parser. dcp_chapter_measure.py runs four signals and a wider parser: widening moves chapters out of UNREADABLE into a real verdict (so INCOMPLETE legitimately rises), and signals 2-4 can find faults in a chapter signal 1 called OK (so OK legitimately falls). Gating the new numbers against these would fail on exactly the work it exists to protect. Kept as provenance; never gated on.

ratchet.compared_against: this code against itself, run N vs run N-1 - never against frozen_signal1
